title: Average cost of full k-coloring
coverageNote: Two supplied records in one primary paper; randomized and deterministic upper statements remain separately inspectable. This is a bounded source review.

marcussen-pyne-rubinfeld-shapira-tauber-.title: Graph k-Coloring in Average Sublinear Time
marcussen-pyne-rubinfeld-shapira-tauber-.publicationEvidence: The author paper record states FOCS 2026.

verifiedRecords.output: Explicit color for every vertex; n vertex–color assignments. Unused colors are allowed.
verifiedRecords.graph: Undirected simple labeled graph on [n], promised k-colorable; k is known and at least 2.
verifiedRecords.oracle: Adjacency-matrix Pair(u,v) query answers whether an edge exists, at unit cost.
verifiedRecords.distribution: Uniform over all labeled k-colorable graphs on [n]. This is not a planted-partition distribution or G(n,p).
verifiedRecords.displayBound: Randomized O(nk); deterministic Õ(nk) average runtime
verifiedRecords.queryComplexity: Randomized O(nk); deterministic Õ(nk) average pair queries, implied by the corresponding runtime bounds
verifiedRecords.theorem: Theorems 1–2; §1.1 matrix-access statement and §§5.2–5.3 correctness/runtime proofs
verifiedRecords.probability: Zero error: every k-colorable input and every random string produce a proper full coloring. Runtime is averaged over the random input and, for the randomized algorithm, its coins. FAIL occurs only inside subroutines; exhaustive fallback completes the coloring.
assumptions: Known n and k; 2 ≤ k ≤ n^(1/37).
Input G is uniformly distributed over all labeled k-colorable graphs on [n] for the average complexity statement.
The algorithms must output a proper coloring on every promised graph, not merely with high probability over G.
Randomized average is E_{G∼U} E_r T(G,r); deterministic average is E_{G∼U} T(G).
One matrix-entry query costs constant time. Thus query count is bounded above by total runtime.
Internal failure triggers further stages and ultimately exhaustive search; external output is a full coloring, never FAIL.
verifiedRecords.notes: These are average-input bounds, not worst-case runtime guarantees and not per-vertex LCA bounds. The tilde hides polylog(n); no particular logarithmic exponent is inferred. k is a colorability promise, not maximum degree or a claim that every color must be used.

verifiedRecords.probability: Requires worst-case correctness: for every k-colorable input and every random string the algorithm outputs a proper full k-coloring. Applies to deterministic and zero-error randomized algorithms, not an unqualified bounded-error model.
assumptions: Known n and k; 2 ≤ k ≤ n^(1/3).
The output must be a proper k-coloring of every promised graph, for every fixed random string.
In the pair-query model, fewer than the required number of inspected entries leave a transcript compatible with another k-colorable graph on which the same output fails.
The bound holds per input and per random string; averaging over U and/or coins preserves it.
k=1 is excluded: an edgeless graph is promised and no adjacency queries are needed to color it.
verifiedRecords.notes: This strengthens the original average-runtime wording. The proof directly bounds matrix queries and hence time. Its larger k-range is shown beyond the upper-bound range, without implying that this source supplies an algorithm there. The theorem also discusses unsorted-list access, but the figure restricts to matrix pair queries. No NP-hardness assumption is needed.

sourceVerification.notes: Randomized O(nk) and deterministic Õ(nk) total average runtime through k≤n^(1/37). Unit-cost pair access implies the same query upper bounds. Zero-error lower bound applies on every input/random string through k≤n^(1/3). Full algorithms always finish with a coloring; no external FAIL. Appendix A LCA bounds are not included.
